evidence.finding: Monitoring recorded intermittent call-processing delays across all queues at 09:15.
Mean service level fell from 88.87% before the incident to 29.16% afterward, dropping from 77.38% at 09:00 to 34.78% at 09:15.
Mean ASA increased from 26.27 seconds before 09:15 to 113.87 seconds afterward, a 333.47% rise.
Post-incident offered calls averaged only 2.07% above forecast and were 7.59% below forecast at the 09:15 onset.
All 49 scheduled agents remained logged in; productive staffing and adherence slightly improved after 09:15.
Every visible queue experienced a material service-level decline and ASA increase with unchanged queue staffing, matching the event's all-queue scope.
Independent recalculation matched every reported interval exactly, with a maximum difference of 0.0 percentage points.

primary_root_cause_detail: An all-queue voice-platform degradation at 09:15 caused intermittent call-processing delays and reduced throughput. The event coincided with the severe service-level step-down and ASA escalation. Mild below-target performance at 08:45–09:00 preceded the event, but does not explain the much larger sustained degradation from 09:15 onward.
recommended_actions: Escalate the 09:15 voice-platform degradation to the platform owner and preserve platform, signaling, and call-processing logs.
Validate recovery across all queues using ASA, answer throughput, abandonment, and service level—not platform health alone.
Apply incident routing or failover procedures when all-queue call-processing latency is detected.
Review the mild 08:45–09:00 load pressure separately and confirm adequate operating buffer around forecast staffing requirements.

rejected_hypotheses.reason: Demand was near forecast and below forecast at the exact 09:15 deterioration.
Scheduled and logged-in staffing remained constant, while productive staffing slightly increased.
Post-event AHT was 0.24% below its pre-event mean and 0.23% below forecast.
Degradation affected all queues despite unchanged queue staffing, rather than remaining localized.
Reported service level matched the specified formula in every interval.

stakeholder_summary: The severe service failure was most likely caused by an all-queue voice-platform incident beginning at 09:15. Service level fell to a 29.16% post-event average and ASA more than quadrupled despite stable staffing, near-forecast demand, stable AHT, and valid reporting.
